State and local government employee defined benefit pension funds

source: Federal Reserve Board, Financial Accounts of the United States (Z.1), table F4_5_s (amounts outstanding) and F4_5_t_tu (transactions, not seasonally adjusted), one line per holding sector
note: The share of each owner is of everything outstanding. Net bought is the Federal Reserve's quarterly net purchases; price and other changes is the change in holdings minus what was bought, which is mostly price moves. The Fed carries Treasury, agency, municipal and corporate bond totals at face value and most holders at market value, which is part of its published gap. Mortgages are loans secured on homes, apartment buildings, offices and farms, owed by households and businesses. The mortgages held by the agency mortgage pools and by the issuers of asset-backed securities are the loans behind mortgage-backed bonds that this tab also counts as the bonds themselves, so in the world ledger that part is counted twice, once as the loan and once as the bond, and the ledger shows how much. Technical detail: the table's own total line is used, not the four kinds of mortgage printed beside it, and the private depository institutions line is left out because it is the sum of the banks' and credit unions' own lines.
